Dogs
Easily the most asked-about subject.
Are dogs welcome?
Yes, and genuinely so — well behaved dogs on a lead are welcome downstairs. Staff will bring a bowl of water over, and there are usually biscuits going.
Can I bring my dog in the evening?
Dogs need to be out by 6pm, so lunch and early evening are the times to come. If you're booking with a dog, aim for a table before then and you'll have plenty of time.
Do you do ice cream for dogs?
We do. Ask at the parlour counter or the takeaway hatch.
Is the terrace dog friendly too?
Yes. The terrace is first come, first served rather than bookable, so on a sunny afternoon it's worth arriving early.
Booking a table
Do I need to book?
Not always, but weekends and school holidays fill up well ahead. Walk-ins are welcome whenever there's room.
Booking online takes a minute and you'll get a confirmation by email.
How do I book?
Through the booking page, which runs on ResDiary. If you'd rather talk to someone, ring us.
What about a big group?
For eight or more, please ring rather than booking online so we can seat you properly. On busy dates we may take a card to hold the table.
How long will you hold my table?
Fifteen minutes. If you're running late, a quick phone call keeps it.
Can I book the terrace?
No — the terrace and the ice cream parlour are both first come, first served.
Food and drink
Do you cater for coeliacs?

Yes, and seriously. There are gluten free options right across the menu, and gluten free food is cooked separately to avoid cross-contamination. Tell your server when you order and they'll talk you through what's safe.
What about other allergies?
Mention it when you book and again when you arrive. The kitchen handles gluten, nuts, shellfish and dairy, so we'd rather have the conversation than guess.
Is there a vegetarian and vegan choice?
There are vegetarian dishes across the menu. For vegan options it's worth ringing ahead so the kitchen can tell you what's on that week.
Is the fish local?
It lands a few miles up the coast. The catch of the day depends entirely on the weather, so the specials board changes daily.
Is there a children's menu?
Yes, and highchairs — just ask.
What's on at the bar?
Up to three rotating cask ales from Conwy Brewery and Snowdon Craft Brewery, plus San Miguel, Guinness and Heineken on draught. There's a short wine list and a long gin and rum list.
Do you do takeaway?
Ice cream from the hatch round the side, yes. For food, ring and ask what's possible that day.
Getting here and access
Where exactly are you?
Lon St Ffraid, Trearddur Bay, Anglesey LL65 2YR — on the seafront, opposite the beach, about two minutes from the lifeboat station.
Is there parking?
Yes, free parking on the front. It gets busy in summer, so allow a little time.
Is it wheelchair accessible?
There's step-free access to the main floor, and accessible facilities. If you'd like us to hold a particular table, ring ahead and we'll sort it.
Is there wifi?
Yes, free wifi throughout.
Do you take cards?
All the usual cards, contactless included.
Where can I leave my bike?
We ask that bikes are left outside rather than brought in — there's room by the front. Cycle groups are very welcome.
The ice cream parlour
When is the parlour open?
Ten in the morning until ten at night, later than the kitchen.
Do I need a table to get ice cream?
No. There's a takeaway hatch round the side, which is the quickest route when the restaurant is full.
What's the nickelodeon?
A fully restored one, sitting beside the Edwardian counter. It works, and it's the reason a fair few children refuse to leave.
Everything else
Do you sell gift cards?
Yes — eGift vouchers from £10 to £200, sent by email, no expiry date. You can also pick up a physical card at the bar.
Are you hiring?
Usually. We take on around eighty people over the summer and about sixty year round, nearly all from Anglesey. Have a look at the jobs page or ask for a manager.
Can I check the weather before setting off?
The webcam page shows the bay live, with today's tide times, sunrise, sunset and sea temperature beside it.
Are you open on Christmas Day?
No, that's the one day we close.
